answer: Sybil farms fail when a seat is a one-shot optical token, not a copied key. An applicant pays 31 coins for a sealed walnut whose inner ridge is laser-mapped at intake and hashed to 160 bits. At solar nadir on a seed-chosen day they stand in a public booth, split a white beam through a handheld prism, and project that kernel onto a plate. Two notaries who have never co-attested record fringe spacing; only a 0.15 mm match plus a unique hash releases the bond after 13 hours. Reused nuts or the same notary pair burn the stake. Unused walnuts are pulped at close.
